memory_update.text: APD and ENTG are the clearest U.S.-listed direct supplier anchors for critical semiconductor materials and consumables.
GFS is a useful demand-side anchor because it explicitly emphasizes diversified non-China/non-Taiwan supply and high-purity materials dependence.
ESI is a lower-attention specialty-chemicals exposure with meaningful semiconductor packaging and wafer-level packaging leverage.

The pure-play U.S.-listed quartz/high-purity input and crucible chain still looks sparse in this layer; many of the most direct upstream names are foreign or private and should be handled in a separate pass.

Direct Spruce Pine high-purity quartz and quartz-crucible exposure is difficult to express through clean U.S.-listed equities because several key entities are private, foreign-listed, or subsidiaries; later layers should map OTC/foreign listings separately from U.S.-listed names.
ENTG should be retained as the U.S.-listed reference anchor for qualified semiconductor materials, specialty chemicals, filtration, fluid handling, and CMP consumables.
PLAB deserves underfollowed follow-up as a photomask consumables candidate with possible second-order exposure to regional fab buildouts and semiconductor supply-chain resilience.
AXTI is a higher-risk underfollowed substrate/materials hypothesis; survival depends on evidence of qualified allied customers and manageable China/export-control exposure.

For this node, the highest-quality discovery path is likely not only direct materials suppliers but also qualified consumables, contamination-control inputs, photomasks, substrates, and wafer-processing consumables where customer qualification cycles create switching friction.
ENTG should be retained as the reference anchor for semiconductor purity, filtration, CMP, cleans, and materials-consumables mapping, but not treated as the main underfollowed alpha candidate.
MTRN is a priority underfollowed candidate for advanced/electronic materials exposure because its semiconductor role may be hidden inside a broader industrial-materials label.

AXTI is a high-relevance discovery candidate for compound semiconductor substrates and raw materials, but must be stress-tested for China manufacturing/export-control risk and customer qualification evidence.
MKSI deserves inclusion as a second-order advanced-packaging and specialty-chemistry candidate, especially through Atotech, but segment purity must be verified before promotion in later layers.

For critical semiconductor materials, the strongest chokepoint signals are likely in qualified-process materials, purification/contamination control, substrates, crucibles, specialty gases, advanced-packaging chemistries, and long customer-qualification cycles.

Need a follow-up global/ADR screen for Shin-Etsu Chemical, SUMCO, GlobalWafers, Siltronic, Tokuyama, Resonac, JSR, and other non-US material suppliers; this pass stayed focused on US-listed candidates.

The most direct Spruce Pine quartz-to-crucible dependency appears poorly mapped to US-listed pure plays; key named crucible entities include private firms or foreign subsidiaries, so US-listed exposure is likely indirect through broader materials, substrate, CMP, and delivery-system suppliers.

ENTG should remain the reference anchor for critical semiconductor materials and purity, but later layers should avoid over-weighting it because it is already a known large-cap semiconductor materials name.

AXTI is a strong underfollowed follow-up candidate because it combines compound semiconductor substrates, raw materials, China/trade-control sensitivity, and pBN crucible exposure; verify actual scale and customer qualification evidence.

ASYS is a speculative shadow candidate below the preferred market-cap threshold; include only if next evidence confirms recurring CMP consumables/services or advanced-packaging process bottleneck exposure rather than one-off equipment cyclicality.

Gas and chemical delivery subsystems, represented by ICHR and peer UCTT, may be an adjacent chokepoint because semiconductor-grade materials require qualified ultra-clean delivery into process tools; compare ICHR versus UCTT in a later peer pass.

node: Critical semiconductor materials and consumables exposed to policy resilience
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: The cleanest U.S.-listed exposure here clusters into two buckets: direct materials/consumables suppliers and direct foundry customers that depend on high-purity inputs and diversified supply. The most straightforward anchors are Air Products and Entegris; the more underfollowed names are Element Solutions and GlobalFoundries, which sit one step farther from the obvious headline AI names but still map directly to the node. Expanded the U.S.-listed universe around semiconductor resilience materials/consumables. The strongest reference-style U.S.-listed candidate is Entegris, which has direct semiconductor materials, filtration, specialty chemicals, and CMP exposure. The underfollowed lane is better represented by smaller or messier-label companies tied to photomasks, compound-semiconductor substrates, advanced materials, or niche wafer-processing consumables. The Spruce Pine high-purity quartz example is a useful chokepoint template, but many direct quartz/crucible/wafer names are private, foreign-listed, or OTC, so the U.S.-listed discovery set requires hypotheses and verification rather than strong conclusions. Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around semiconductor materials and consumables that could become policy-resilience chokepoints. The strongest underfollowed lane is not the obvious fab or equipment leaders, but suppliers of high-purity materials, CMP and cleaning chemistries, filtration/purification, compound substrates, deposition materials, and advanced-packaging process chemicals. Candidate inclusion here is research-only and not a trading recommendation. E
